description: Checklist-review cases for the Meridian Code Academy corpus. Each scenario is evaluated item-by-item against one or more documents. Item results: PASS, FAIL, NEEDS_INFO. Several cases require mapping a breach to the correct sanction tier - the showcase capability for this corpus.

cases.scenario: During an exam, a student is found with their phone in their pocket and is then caught glancing at it.

items.reason: Devices must be switched off and stored in the bag; a phone in the pocket breaches this.
Looking at a phone during the exam is defined as cheating.
Cheating is a Tier 3 offense, referred to the Disciplinary Board.

cases.scenario: A student keeps a can of soda at their cluster workstation and leaves the chair and keyboard untidy when they leave.

items.reason: Holding a non-water drink at a cluster workstation is a Tier 1 offense (minimum 3 hours community service).
Failing to tidy the workstation is also a Tier 1 offense.

cases.scenario: A student's project app stores API responses on a personal server and exposes an endpoint that lets a non-student friend query that data.

items.reason: The API is read-only and local storage of API data is prohibited without end-user consent.
Giving a non-authorized third party access and making data available outside the MCA network are prohibited practices.
Whether the app encrypts data in transit and at rest is not stated, so the security-measures requirement cannot be judged.

cases.scenario: A security project subject lists only host TARGET-A and runs from 1-7 March. A student scans TARGET-B on 9 March directly from their laptop with no isolation.

items.reason: TARGET-B is not a listed target; acting against it is a Tier 3 offense.
9 March is outside the 1-7 March window.
The action was not contained (no isolated VM).

cases.scenario: An automated bot scrapes the MCA public website at high volume, and the same actor repeatedly tries to log into an account that is not theirs.

items.reason: Automated scraping without authorization and disrupting the site are prohibited uses.
Attempting to gain unauthorized access to another account is a prohibited use.

cases.scenario: A student sets their intranet password to 'meridian2026' (12 characters, lowercase letters and digits only).

items.reason: The password is 12 characters, meeting the minimum length.
It contains no uppercase letter, so it fails the character-class requirement.
